newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia seeks foreign car component investors.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seeks foreign car component investors.

text.p: Indonesia plans to allow temporary 100 percent foreign ownership for companies that invest in the country's car component industry, Research and Techonology Minister Jusuf Habibie said on Tuesday.

"Investors can begin with 100 percent ownership, with the provision that they find a local partner in not too long a time. The local partner can then take a 10 percent stake," Habibie told reporters after meeting President Suharto.

Habibie gave no details about the conditions of investment or how long foreign companies would be given to find a local partner, adding only that the Trade and Industry Minister would be responsible for the implementation of the policy.
He said the development of a local components industry had been slow because of the lack of investment.
Habibie, who recently visited Turkey, Italy, Spain and Egypt, said investors from those countries had shown an interest in investing in the car component industry.
"It is expected to support the Timor car which must contain local components," he said, giving no further details.

PT Timor Putra National, a company controlled by Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, last year was given tax and tariff breaks from the government to produce the Timor car in association with Kia Motors Corp of South Korea.
The government gave the concession on the condition that the Timor met local content targets over three years and it said the policy was designed to boost the local car component industry.
